prompt.adult: Paul says not to grieve the Spirit. For what day were believers sealed?
prompt.child: Paul says God’s Spirit has put a seal on believers. For what day?
prompt.teen: Ephesians 4:30: “by whom you were sealed for” what?
prompt.older: According to Ephesians 4:30, for what were believers sealed?

verses.text: And do not grieve the Holy Spirit of God, by whom you were sealed for the day of redemption.

explanation.child: Look at the last words of verse 30.
explanation.teen: 4:30 gives a warning and says by whom and for what you were sealed. Read the end.
explanation.older: It follows “by whom you were sealed for” in 4:30.

teaching.extended_explanation: 4:29 says to let no corrupt word proceed out of your mouth. 4:31 says to put away all bitterness.
teaching.takeaway: Believers were sealed for the day of redemption.

prompt.adult: Paul tells the Ephesians to be something “as dear children.” What should they be?
prompt.child: Paul gives God’s dear children a command. What does he tell them to be?
prompt.older: According to Ephesians 5:1, what are believers to be, as dear children?

verses.text: Therefore be imitators of God as dear children.

explanation.teen: 5:1 gives one command and a comparison. Read the command.

teaching.extended_explanation: 5:2 says to walk in love. 5:8 calls them to walk as children of light.
teaching.takeaway: Be imitators of God as dear children.

prompt.adult: Paul tells believers to put away lying and speak truth with a neighbor. According to 4:25, what reason does he give? Because we are what?
prompt.child: Paul says to stop lying and speak the truth. What reason does he give?
prompt.teen: Ephesians 4:25: speak truth with his neighbor, “for we are” what?
prompt.older: According to Ephesians 4:25, what are believers, as the reason to speak truth?

verses.text: Therefore, putting away lying, “Let each one of you speak truth with his neighbor,” for we are members of one another.
“Be angry, and do not sin”: do not let the sun go down on your wrath,

explanation.child: Look at the last words of verse 25.
explanation.teen: 4:25 gives a command, a quotation, and a reason. Read the reason.

teaching.extended_explanation: 4:26 says, “Be angry, and do not sin.” 4:24 speaks of putting on the new man.
teaching.takeaway: We speak truth because we are members of one another.

prompt.adult: Paul warns that the wrath of God comes upon the sons of disobedience. According to 5:6, with what should no one deceive you?
prompt.child: Paul warns believers not to be fooled. With what does he say no one should deceive you?
prompt.teen: Ephesians 5:6: “Let no one deceive you with” what?
prompt.older: According to Ephesians 5:6, with what must no one deceive believers?

verses.text: Let no one deceive you with empty words, for because of these things the wrath of God comes upon the sons of disobedience.
Therefore do not be partakers with them.

explanation.child: Look right after “deceive you with” in verse 6.
explanation.teen: 5:6 gives a warning, then a reason about wrath. Read the end of the warning.
explanation.older: It follows “Let no one deceive you with” in 5:6.

teaching.extended_explanation: 5:7 says not to be partakers with them. 5:8 says you were once darkness, but now you are light in the Lord.
teaching.takeaway: Let no one deceive you with empty words.

prompt.adult: Paul tells believers to speak to one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs. According to 5:19, what are they doing in their heart to the Lord, along with singing?
prompt.child: Paul says to sing to the Lord. What else does he say to do in the heart?
prompt.teen: Ephesians 5:19: “singing and” what, to the Lord?
prompt.older: According to Ephesians 5:19, what goes with singing in the heart?

verses.text: speaking to one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody in your heart to the Lord,
giving thanks always for all things to God the Father in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ,

explanation.child: Look right after “singing and” in verse 19.
explanation.teen: 5:19 lists three kinds of songs, then two actions and where. Read the second action.

teaching.extended_explanation: 5:20 adds giving thanks always to God the Father. 5:17 says to understand what the will of the Lord is.
teaching.takeaway: Believers sing and are making melody in their heart to the Lord.

prompt.adult: In 5:25 Paul says Christ loved the church and gave Himself for her. In 5:2, Christ’s offering and sacrifice to God were for what?
prompt.child: Paul says Jesus gave Himself as an offering to God. What does Paul call it?
prompt.teen: Ephesians 5:2: “an offering and a sacrifice to God for” what?
prompt.older: Read with 5:25, what does 5:2 call Christ’s sacrifice to God?

verses.text: And walk in love, as Christ also has loved us and given Himself for us, an offering and a sacrifice to God for a sweet-smelling aroma.
Husbands, love your wives, just as Christ also loved the church and gave Himself for her,

explanation.child: Look at the last words of verse 2.
explanation.teen: 5:25 tells husbands how Christ loved; 5:2 says to walk in love, how Christ gave Himself, and for what. Read the end.
explanation.older: It follows “an offering and a sacrifice to God for” in 5:2.

teaching.extended_explanation: 5:2 begins, “And walk in love.” 5:26 says He did it to sanctify and cleanse her.
teaching.takeaway: Christ gave Himself for a sweet-smelling aroma.

prompt.adult: 4:24 says to put on the new man, created in true righteousness and holiness. In 5:27, Christ presents a glorious church not having spot or what?
prompt.child: Paul says Christ will present the church to Himself. Besides a spot, what will it not have?
prompt.older: Read with 4:24, what besides spot does 5:27 say the church will not have?

verses.text: and that you put on the new man which was created according to God, in true righteousness and holiness.
that He might present her to Himself a glorious church, not having spot or wrinkle or any such thing, but that she should be holy and without blemish.

explanation.child: Look right after “spot or” in verse 27.
explanation.teen: 4:24 describes the new man; 5:27 says how Christ presents the church, lists what she lacks, then says what she is. Read the list.
explanation.older: It follows “not having spot or” in 5:27.

teaching.extended_explanation: 5:27 ends by saying she should be holy. 4:23 speaks of being renewed in the spirit of your mind.
teaching.takeaway: The church will not have spot or wrinkle.

prompt.adult: 6:4 tells fathers not to provoke their children to wrath. In 4:31, along with bitterness, wrath, anger, and clamor, what must be put away?
prompt.child: Paul lists things to get rid of: bitterness, wrath, anger, clamor, and one more before malice. What is the fifth?
prompt.teen: Ephesians 4:31: “Let all bitterness, wrath, anger, clamor, and” what “be put away from you”?
prompt.older: Read with 6:4, what does 4:31 list after clamor?

verses.text: Let all bitterness, wrath, anger, clamor, and evil speaking be put away from you, with all malice.
And you, fathers, do not provoke your children to wrath, but bring them up in the training and admonition of the Lord.

explanation.child: Look right after “clamor, and” in verse 31.
explanation.teen: 6:4 warns fathers; 4:31 lists five things to put away, then adds malice. Read the fifth.
explanation.older: It follows “Let all bitterness, wrath, anger, clamor, and” in 4:31.

teaching.extended_explanation: 4:29 says to let no corrupt word proceed out of your mouth. 6:4 also tells fathers how to bring up their children.
teaching.takeaway: Evil speaking must be put away, with all malice.
